```text
skills\notion\SKILL.md:197:python3 notion_request.py PATCH /v1/blocks/{page_id}/children append-blocks.json

rg "curl -X|NOTION_KEY=|\$\(cat|; curl|\\\s*$" skills/notion/SKILL.md
All requests need the `Authorization`, `Notion-Version`, and usually `Content-Type` headers. Use `NOTION_API_KEY`; do not create a shell-local alias such as `NOTION_KEY=$(cat ...)`.
Strict exec allowlist note: avoid examples shaped like `NOTION_KEY=...; curl ...`, command substitution, shell chaining, and line continuations. In `security=allowlist` with `ask=off`, those forms can be denied as an allowlist miss even when the underlying `curl` binary is allowlisted. Prefer a direct executable invocation with secrets already supplied in the environment, or a small file-backed helper run through an allowlisted interpreter.
```

- Observed result after fix: The patched Notion skill presents the allowlist-safe `NOTION_API_KEY` setup and direct helper-command examples for every common operation. The old executable examples no longer include multi-line `curl -X ...`, `NOTION_KEY=...; curl ...`, or command-substitution setup; the remaining `curl`/`NOTION_KEY` mentions are warnings describing what to avoid.
- What was not tested: No live Notion API request was sent because that would require a real Notion workspace/integration secret. The changed behavior is documentation guidance and command shape, so validation focused on the bundled skill content and docs checks.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this patch, `skills/notion/SKILL.md` told users to run `NOTION_KEY=$(cat ~/.config/notion/api_key)` and then use multi-line `curl` commands with `$NOTION_KEY`, which matches the allowlist-miss shape reported in #59235.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: The Notion skill docs predated the stricter allowlist guidance and used shell-local variable assignment, command substitution, and multi-line `curl` examples even though strict allowlist parsing can reject shell control/expansion shapes before reaching the underlying executable.
- Missing detection / guardrail: The skill doc did not call out strict exec allowlist constraints or prefer a direct executable/helper shape for secure configurations.
- Contributing context (if known): Prior fix attempts (#59254 and #59870) were closed unmerged, and the current bundled skill still contained the reported pattern.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:

  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test

- Target test or file: `skills/notion/SKILL.md`
- Scenario the test should lock in: The Notion skill should not recommend shell-substitution/chained `curl` examples for strict allowlist users.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: This is a docs-only issue; the existing exec-approval tests already cover why command substitution, shell chaining, and line continuations are allowlist-hostile.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): `src/infra/exec-approvals-analysis.test.ts` covers the parser constraints; this PR updates the skill docs to respect them.
- If no new test is added, why not: No runtime behavior changed; markdown formatting and docs listing are the relevant local gates.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users reading the bundled Notion skill now get allowlist-friendly setup and request examples instead of a shell-wrapped `curl` workflow that can fail under strict exec policies.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
Notion skill docs -> NOTION_KEY=$(cat ...) + multi-line curl -> strict allowlist miss risk

After:
Notion skill docs -> NOTION_API_KEY + file-backed python3 helper -> direct allowlist-friendly command shape
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No runtime change`; docs now point at the existing `skills.entries.notion.apiKey` / `NOTION_API_KEY` secret path instead of suggesting a separate shell-local alias.

target.title: fix(acp): honor tagVisibility.agent_thought_chunk for thought-stream events
target.body:
## Summary

Honor the operator-tunable `tagVisibility.agent_thought_chunk` flag for ACP thought-stream `text_delta` events. Closes catalog finding #12.

## Bug detail

Wire probe captured 2 `agent_thought_chunk` sessionUpdates per turn from copilot's ACP runtime. The deployed openclaw config set `tagVisibility.agent_thought_chunk: true`, but the operator never saw the thoughts in any channel. The projector at `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts:408-411` had a hard `event.stream !== "output"` guard that ran BEFORE the `isAcpTagVisible` check, so the operator-tunable visibility flag was structurally unreachable for thought-stream events.

## How to reproduce

Unit-level repro in this branch before the fix commit (`f0180a023c`):

```bash
git checkout f0180a023c
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.thought-chunk-delivery.test.ts
# Expected: 'delivers thought chunks when tagVisibility.agent_thought_chunk=true' FAILS
```

After the fix commit (`379320c173`) the same test passes.

## Root cause

`src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts:408-411` (pre-fix):

```ts
if (event.type === \"text_delta\") {
  if (event.stream && event.stream !== \"output\") {
    return; // drops ALL non-\"output\" streams unconditionally, including \"thought\"
  }
  if (!isAcpTagVisible(settings, event.tag)) {
    return;
  }
}
```

The `acpx` translator faithfully tags the event with `stream: \"thought\"`; the projector unconditionally discarded it before consulting visibility settings.

## Fix approach

Reorder the guards: `isAcpTagVisible` runs FIRST and is authoritative; only if visibility is denied does the function return. The stream check is then narrowed so that \"output\" and \"thought\" streams both fall through to delivery, while other unknown streams (e.g., a hypothetical `stream: \"diagnostic\"`) still drop. Default behavior unchanged: `tagVisibility.agent_thought_chunk: false` (default) keeps thought events hidden.

## Tests

- **Red test (now GREEN):** `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.thought-chunk-delivery.test.ts` — 3 scenarios cover default-hidden, visibility-true (the fix), and output-stream control.
- **Adjacent suite:** `src/auto-reply/reply/` — 1538 tests pass / 0 fail (115 files).

## Catalog reference

Catalog finding: #12. Investigation lives in branch `edpiva/acp-native-session-investigation` (not yet upstream) at `docs/plans/2026-05-08-acp-findings-catalog.md`.

## Verification commands

\`\`\`bash
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.thought-chunk-delivery.test.ts   # GREEN
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/                                              # 1538 pass / 0 fail
\`\`\`

## Notes for reviewers

The new guard correctly drops unknown-stream events (e.g., `stream: \"diagnostic\"`) regardless of `tagVisibility`, but no test exercises that path explicitly. The behavior is the desired one — coverage gap only, not a wrong fix. Happy to add a fourth test case if you want it.

---

## Live behavior repro (deployed container)

**Container:** `codeclaw-openclaw:clean` running OpenClaw 2026.5.6 (`e9d4a0a`)
**PII note:** UUIDs are random; nothing to redact in this slice.

### Operator opted into thought delivery, copilot emitted thought events, projector dropped them all

Live config in the container:

```
$ docker exec codeclaw-openclaw jq '.acp.stream.tagVisibility' /home/codeclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json
{
  "tool_call": true,
  "tool_call_update": true,
  "agent_thought_chunk": true,
  "plan": true
}
```

Operator has `agent_thought_chunk: true` set (i.e., wants thoughts delivered).

Copilot's `events.jsonl` for the relevant ACP session shows the events arrived on the wire:

```
$ docker exec codeclaw-openclaw grep -c agent_thought_chunk \
    /home/codeclaw/.copilot/session-state/882435ee-…/events.jsonl
2
```

Pre-fix, those events were silently dropped at `acp-projector.ts:408-411` because the unconditional `event.stream !== "output"` guard ran BEFORE `isAcpTagVisible` could consult the operator-tunable visibility flag. Operator never saw a thought chunk, even after explicitly opting in.

After this PR (fix `379320c173` + coverage `bdf2df35ab`), `isAcpTagVisible` runs first and is authoritative, then the stream allow-list narrows to `"output" | "thought"`. Hypothetical unknown streams (e.g., `"diagnostic"`) still drop regardless of `tagVisibility` — covered by the 4th test added in the cleanup commit.

## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).

- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
```

target.body:
## Summary

Adds a recipe page documenting how to use existing OpenClaw primitives (custom `baseUrl`, eager SecretRef snapshot) to build an external auth-injection proxy that closes the agent-self-read gap acknowledged in #11829 and #10659.

The page does **not** propose any core change. It documents a pattern users can apply today.

## Why now

`@steipete`'s 2026-04-26 review on #10659 explicitly framed current SecretRef + redaction + plugin hooks as **partial** hardening, and noted that native masked-secret / credential-provider boundaries are unbuilt. PR #9271 attempted a full in-core proxy and was closed unmerged at 15.9K LOC. PRs #12839 and #22744 followed similar fates.

That leaves users hitting this issue with no documented workaround. This recipe gives them one — focused on the surface OpenClaw already exposes — without staking a position on what the eventual native solution should look like.

## Field validation

Implemented and running on a 21-tenant Badclaw deployment (Hetzner CPX41) for the Anthropic provider. End-to-end verification:

- Agent container has no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env, in `/run/secrets/`, or anywhere on its filesystem.
- A live chat completion through the proxy returns 200 in 1326ms (Anthropic-side latency dominates; localhost-hop overhead measured at <1ms).
- Proxy access logs show source-IP-based tenant identification working as designed.

Reference implementation linked from the page: https://github.com/coletebou/Badland/tree/master/badclaw/services/auth-proxy (~150 LOC stdlib-only Node, MIT-licensed).

## What this PR doesn't do

- Doesn't add a built-in proxy. That's a much larger conversation (#9271 territory) and would need maintainer alignment on shape.
- Doesn't change SecretRef semantics, OAuth refresh, or any runtime behavior.
- Doesn't conflict with the active plugin-SDK work in #59165 / #72548 — those operate on a different bridge (credential resolution, not request rewriting).

target.title: feat(exec): inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID env vars for child processes
target.body:
## Summary
Inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` environment variables into child processes spawned by the exec tool, allowing scripts and skills to reliably identify the current session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

Supersedes #68859 with full coverage including node-host execution, regression tests, and docs updates.

Closes #66705

## Problem
Currently, skills and scripts executed via exec have no reliable way to determine which session or agent they belong to. While the model can pass these identifiers as parameters, this approach is prone to hallucination errors where the model may provide incorrect values.

This blocks workflows where a child process needs to register a callback or webhook that routes back to the originating session.

## Solution
Automatically inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` into the environment of child processes spawned by exec, across all execution paths.

### Changes

**Core injection:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` — inject both vars in `runExecProcess` (`shellRuntimeEnv`)
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` — inject both vars in `shellRuntimeEnv` after sanitization for `host=node` execution
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts` — pass `agentId` through gateway allowlist path

**Type updates:**
- Added `agentId?: string` to `runExecProcess` opts type

**Documentation:**
- `docs/help/environment.md` — document both new env vars
- `docs/tools/exec.md` — note session/agent injection for all exec hosts

**Tests:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts` — 6 new tests covering gateway injection, user env override prevention, and empty-string clearing semantics
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — updated sanitizer allowlist test to verify trusted var injection
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` — removed stale test (gateway no longer injects vars into `requestedEnv`)

## Testing
- [x] Local gateway execution (host=gateway)
- [x] Sandbox execution (host=sandbox) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] PTY mode (pty=true) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] Node-host execution (host=node) — unit tests in invoke-system-run.test.ts
- [x] Override semantics — user env cannot override trusted values
- [x] Clearing semantics — empty string when no agent/session defaults provided

## Usage Example
```python
import os
session_key = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY")
agent_id = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID")
```

## Backward Compatibility
Fully backward compatible:
- Variables always set (empty string when not available), avoiding stale-value issues
- Trusted values override any user-provided env overrides with the same names
- No existing behavior changed

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID environment variables into exec child processes so skills and scripts can reliably identify their session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw 2026.4.2, macOS arm64, gateway mode

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Built and ran OpenClaw gateway with the patched code
2. Created a minimal test skill at workspace/skills/test-env-injection/ that prints both environment variables
3. Executed the skill script via the exec tool within a main agent session
4. Captured the console output

**Evidence after fix**:
```bash
$ python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/test-env-injection/test.py
agent:main:2
main
```

**Observed result after fix**: Both OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID are correctly injected into the exec child process environment. The output matches the expected session key (agent:main:2) and agent id (main).

**What was not tested**: Node-host (host=node) execution path was not tested in a real multi-node setup; only unit tests cover this path.

target.title: fix(exec-policy): accept trusted ~/.openclaw symlink at home boundary
target.body:
Fixes #72572.

## Problem

The exec-approvals symlink hardening from #72377 only relaxed the restriction on the `OPENCLAW_HOME` root itself, so a symlinked `~/.openclaw` immediate child of a real home directory still trips `assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()`:

\`\`\`
Refusing to traverse symlink in exec approvals path: /Users/funjim/.openclaw
\`\`\`

This breaks \`openclaw exec-policy preset yolo\` (and every other exec-policy command) for users who manage their OpenClaw config via GNU Stow, chezmoi, or any other dotfile-managed setup that exposes \`~/.openclaw → ~/dotfiles/openclaw/.openclaw\`.

## Fix

Allow EXACTLY ONE trusted symlink hop at the immediate child of the trusted home root, gated by the same hardening intent as #64050 / #72377:

1. Only the immediate child of the trusted root may be a symlink (deeper symlinks inside the resolved tree remain rejected).
2. The symlink target's realpath must be owned by the current effective user (\`process.geteuid()\`).
3. The symlink target must not be group- or other-writable (mode bits \`0o022\`).
4. After consuming the trusted hop, traversal continues from the realpath target with the original per-segment symlink rejection — a second symlink anywhere below is still rejected.

Permissive on platforms without \`process.geteuid\` (Windows), where the OS ACL model already differs.

\`ensureDir()\` is taught to accept a \`dir\` whose \`lstatSync\` reports a symlink, but only after re-asserting the realpath target is a directory — \`assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()\` already vetted ownership/perms.

## Tests

- **New**: \`accepts a symlinked ~/.openclaw immediate child of the trusted home\` — constructs the exact GNU Stow layout from the issue and verifies the file lands at the realpath target.
- **Updated**: \`refuses to traverse symlinked approvals components below a symlinked home\` — now constructs an unsafe (group-writable) symlink target so the deeper-symlink rejection intent of #72377 is still exercised. The original test became implicitly the same scenario as the new accept-test once the trusted-hop relaxation landed; making the target unsafe keeps the rejection branch under test.

All 18 \`exec-approvals-store\` tests pass; \`pnpm tsgo:test\` clean.

## Diff

+92 / -3 across 2 production files + 1 test file + CHANGELOG.

## Refs

- Original hardening: #64050
- Replaced PR (broader fix): #64663
- Merged narrow replacement: #72377
- This PR strictly broadens #72377 in the safe direction the issue describes.

target.title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command+url transport config (#72111)
target.body:
Closes #72111.

## Problem

When an MCP server config carries **both** a non-empty `command` and a non-empty `url` (e.g. a streamable-http endpoint plus a `command`/`args` pair), the runtime silently picks stdio and drops the HTTP transport. The user sees:

```
MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms
```

The spawned child never speaks JSON-RPC over stdio because the user actually wanted the streamable-http endpoint. The clawsweeper bot triaged this and recommended early rejection over silent fallback.

## Root cause

`resolveMcpTransportConfig` in `src/agents/mcp-transport-config.ts` resolves the stdio launch first when `command` is set, regardless of whether `url` is also set. The 30s timeout that follows is the user-visible symptom; the silent fallback at config-resolution time is the real bug.

## Reproducer

In `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  \"mcp\": {
    \"servers\": {
      \"broken\": {
        \"command\": \"node\",
        \"args\": [\"something.js\"],
        \"url\": \"https://my-mcp.example.com/mcp\"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Run OpenClaw → the `broken` server hangs, then errors with `MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms`. There is no clue in the logs about *which* transport was actually attempted.

## Fix

Reject the ambiguous shape early with a clear diagnostic that names the offending server and the requested transport hint, matching the file's existing \"skipped server X because Y\" diagnostic style and the clawsweeper bot's \"Best possible solution\":

> reject mixed `command` + `url`/HTTP transport configs early with a clear diagnostic and docs/test alignment. The current silent stdio precedence should not remain the user-visible timeout path.

Implementation: when `command` and a non-whitespace `url` are both present, log the warning, return `null` (caller already handles `null` as \"skip this server\"), and let the user fix their config.

Pure stdio configs (no `url`) and pure HTTP configs (no `command`) are unaffected. **Whitespace-only `url`** strings continue to be treated as \"no url\" so stdio still wins, matching the existing trimming in `mcp-stdio.ts`.

Diff: **+17** lines in `mcp-transport-config.ts`, **+52** in tests.

## Verification

```
pnpm vitest run src/agents/mcp-transport-config.test.ts
# 11 passed (7 original + 4 new)

pnpm check
# 0 errors, 0 warnings; all policy guards green
```

## Tests added (4 new)

1. **Mixed config + transport hint** → resolution returns `null`; warning lists both `command` and `url` and the requested transport.
2. **Mixed config without explicit transport hint** → still rejected; warning is informative.
3. **Whitespace-only `url` paired with real `command`** → resolution returns stdio (mirrors `mcp-stdio.ts` trimming).
4. **Sanitized transport in warning** → diagnostic does not leak full URL secrets / query strings.

## Risk notes

- **Behavior change is user-visible**: configs that used to silently fall back to stdio when both `command`+`url` were set now get rejected outright (server skipped, no spawn). That is the bot-blessed shape and matches the issue, but anyone relying on the silent fallback (unlikely — it was the bug) will see a behavior shift on upgrade.
- Did NOT touch `src/agents/mcp-stdio.ts` even though the bot's evidence cites it; the rejection is cleaner at the transport-config layer where both fields are visible together.
- PR collision check: 8 open MCP-related PRs in the repo (#66542, #69417, #69039, #65574, #62134, #64316, #62160, #60005); none touch `mcp-transport-config.ts` validation logic for the mixed shape. Safe to land independently.

target.body:
## Summary

Adds two plugin observability hooks for model failure handling:

- `model_failover`: observes embedded-runner failover decisions, including failed source refs, selected target refs, stage, decision, reason metadata, recoverability, timeout/abort/status flags, and fallback availability.
- `model_failure_terminal`: observes terminal before-reply model failures after all configured attempts are exhausted.

This PR does not change fallback policy, provider retry behavior, context re-injection behavior, command/tool execution, network access, or default user-facing failure copy.

## Current implementation

- Emits `model_failover` from the embedded-runner failover decision path.
- Propagates the selected fallback candidate through direct agent-command runs, Gateway auto-reply runs, and queued follow-up runs before running the embedded agent.
- Emits `model_failure_terminal` after resolving the actual delivered failure reply, so `finalMessage` matches user-visible failure copy.
- Registers both hook names and payload types in the Plugin SDK surface and refreshes the SDK API baseline hash.
- Bounds both failure-path void hooks with default 30s timeout budgets and fail-open behavior.

## Security / compatibility

- New public Plugin SDK hook contract: `model_failover`, `model_failure_terminal`.
- `model_failure_terminal` is conversation-access gated for non-bundled plugins because it can expose delivered failure copy.
- Attempt summaries expose provider/model/reason metadata, not raw provider error blobs.
- Maintainers still need to accept the public hook contract and terminal-failure data boundary before release.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: A real embedded OpenClaw model run should emit `model_failover` when the primary model fails and the runtime selects the configured fallback target. A separate exhausted-model run should emit `model_failure_terminal` after all configured model attempts fail, with `finalMessage` matching the user-visible failure copy and `attempts` summarizing provider/model/reason metadata.
- **Environment tested**: Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS Darwin 25.3.0 arm64, Node `v25.6.0`, pnpm `11.2.2`, PR head `5cd9b674c3b9`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: The proof runner created a temporary workspace, temporary state dir, and a real workspace plugin with `openclaw.plugin.json`. OpenClaw loaded that plugin through the real plugin loader; the plugin registered `api.on("model_failover", ...)` and `api.on("model_failure_terminal", ...)` and wrote hook payloads to a redacted JSONL artifact. Model providers were deterministic local OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints. Scenario 1 returned HTTP 429 from the primary endpoint and a successful SSE canary from fallback. Scenario 2 returned HTTP 429 from both primary and fallback to exhaust all configured model attempts. No external provider token was used.

```bash
OPENCLAW_MODEL_FAILOVER_PROOF_HEAD=$(git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD) node --import tsx .artifacts/model-failover-real-proof.mjs
```

The runtime output confirmed `model_failover` fired after `proof-primary/proof-primary-model` returned HTTP 429, selected `proof-fallback/proof-fallback-model`, and then delivered `PROOF_FALLBACK_CANARY_OK`. The same proof run confirmed the exhausted-model scenario emitted `model_failure_terminal` after both configured attempts failed.
- **Observed result after fix**:
  - `model_failover` reported selected target `proof-fallback/proof-fallback-model`, failed source `proof-primary/proof-primary-model`, `decision: fallback_model`, `failoverReason: rate_limit`, `status: 429`, and `sourceRecoverable: true`.
  - The fallback endpoint was hit and the run delivered `PROOF_FALLBACK_CANARY_OK`.
  - The terminal run hit both `proof-terminal-primary/proof-terminal-primary-model` and `proof-terminal-fallback/proof-terminal-fallback-model`, exhausted all attempts, and emitted `model_failure_terminal` with `kind: all_models_failed`.
  - `model_failure_terminal.finalMessage` was exactly the delivered terminal reply: `⚠️ All models are temporarily rate-limited. Please try again in a few minutes.`
  - Terminal `attempts` contained both failed provider/model summaries with `rate_limit` reasons.
- **Not tested**: Live third-party provider outages were not tested; provider failures were deterministic local HTTP endpoints. Secret-bearing headers were redacted in proof output.

## Regression coverage for the latest review findings

target.title: perf(memory): prewarm explicit local embeddings on gateway startup
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: builtin `memory_search` with explicit `memorySearch.provider = "local"` still pays model/context initialization on the first post-startup search because gateway startup only warmed QMD.
- Why it matters: the first memory-backed reply after a gateway restart absorbs the local embedding cold start instead of the post-attach startup path.
- What changed: extend `startGatewayMemoryBackend` to prewarm builtin local managers by calling `probeEmbeddingAvailability()` after manager creation, and add gateway startup tests for explicit-local, skip, and failure logging paths.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not prewarm `provider = "auto"` or remote embedding providers, so startup avoids new remote network calls or auth/cost side effects.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #70460
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: builtin memory with explicit `memorySearch.provider = "local"` now enters the Gateway startup prewarm path instead of waiting for the first real `memory_search`; prewarm failures are warnings and do not block startup.
- Real environment tested: macOS local checkout, production build output from `pnpm build`, temporary OpenClaw state/workspace, Node invoking the built `dist/server-startup-memory-*.js` module.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran the built startup module with a temporary config using `memory.backend=builtin`, `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider=local`, vector disabled, and a temporary `memory/MEMORY.md` file.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```text

workspace: <temp>/workspace
warn: builtin local memory startup prewarm failed for agent "main": Error: Local embeddings unavailable.
Reason: optional dependency node-llama-cpp is missing (or failed to install).
Detail: Cannot find package 'node-llama-cpp' imported from /Users/tsy/opensouce/openclaw/dist/memory-core-host-engine-embeddings-B374_HhW.js
To enable local embeddings:
1) Use Node 24 (recommended for installs/updates; Node 22 LTS, currently 22.16+, remains supported)
2) Install node-llama-cpp next to the OpenClaw package or source checkout
3) If you use pnpm: pnpm approve-builds (select node-llama-cpp), then pnpm rebuild node-llama-cpp
Or set agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider = "github-copilot" (remote).
Or set agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider = "openai" (remote).
Or set agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider = "gemini" (remote).
Or set agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider = "voyage" (remote).
Or set agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider = "mistral" (remote).
Or set agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider = "deepinfra" (remote).
Or set agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider = "bedrock" (remote).
result: startup hook completed with 1 log event(s)
```

- Observed result after fix: the production startup hook called the builtin local prewarm path for agent `main`, surfaced the real local-provider availability error as a warning, and completed without throwing or blocking startup.
- What was not tested: successful local model load with `node-llama-cpp` installed on this machine; the real setup here verifies the startup/prewarm routing and graceful failure path.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): before this patch, builtin backends were skipped by `startGatewayMemoryBackend` unless the resolved backend was QMD, so this same builtin/local startup path did not call the memory manager prewarm probe.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: post-attach startup only initialized QMD memory, so builtin local memory waited until the first real search to create the manager and load the local embedding context.
- Missing detection / guardrail: gateway startup coverage did not assert builtin explicit-local prewarm behavior or failure logging.
- Contributing context (if known): `purpose: "status"` managers bypass the builtin cache, so a status-only probe would not have helped the first real search.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/gateway/server-startup-memory.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: explicit local builtin memory runs `probeEmbeddingAvailability()` at startup, non-local builtin configs skip startup work, and probe failures degrade to warnings.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it exercises the gateway startup decision point without requiring real local model assets.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing QMD startup tests in the same file.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Gateways using builtin memory with `agents.*.memorySearch.provider = "local"` now shift local embedding cold-start work into post-attach startup, so the first real `memory_search` request avoids paying that initialization cost.
- No behavior change for QMD, `provider = "auto"`, or remote memory embedding providers.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
gateway boot -> first builtin local memory_search -> init local embedding context -> delayed first result

After:
gateway boot -> post-attach startup prewarm -> first builtin local memory_search -> reuse warmed context
```

1. Start the gateway with builtin memory and an explicit local memory provider.
2. Let post-attach startup run.

### Expected

### Actual

target.title: fix(mcp): allow SecretRef values in mcp.servers env and headers [AI-assisted]
target.body:
## Summary

This PR adds SecretRef support to core MCP server configuration so `mcp.servers.*.env.*` and `mcp.servers.*.headers.*` can use SecretInput values in addition to plaintext literals.

Before this change, core `mcp.servers` only accepted primitive literal values on these surfaces, which meant MCP credentials on the built-in config path had to remain plaintext even though other SecretRef-capable surfaces already supported resolved runtime credentials.

## What changed

- allow `SecretInput` values in `mcp.servers.*.env.*`
- allow `SecretInput` values in `mcp.servers.*.headers.*`
- include core MCP env/header targets in command/runtime secret resolution
- resolve only the active MCP transport surface at runtime
- include core MCP env/header targets in the supported SecretRef target registry
- teach `secrets configure` and `secrets audit` to handle MCP env/header targets without promoting generic non-secret literals like URLs and feature flags
- update the MCP and SecretRef docs/matrix to document the supported surface

## Why

This keeps sensitive MCP credentials out of plaintext config while preserving the existing runtime model:

- config stores SecretRefs
- activation resolves active refs into the in-memory runtime snapshot
- spawned MCP processes receive resolved string values at launch time

That is consistent with the rest of OpenClaw’s SecretRef model and removes a real gap on the core `mcp.servers` surface.

## Validation

Passed locally:

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm check`

Passed targeted coverage for the touched surface:

- `src/config/config-misc.test.ts`
- `src/secrets/configure-plan.test.ts`
- `src/secrets/target-registry.docs.test.ts`
- `src/secrets/runtime-core-snapshots.test.ts`
- `src/secrets/runtime-inactive-core-surfaces.test.ts`
- `src/commands/agent.runtime-config.test.ts`
- `src/cli/command-secret-targets.test.ts`
- `src/agents/pi-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`
- targeted `src/secrets/audit.test.ts` coverage for MCP plaintext detection heuristics

Additional functional validation:

- verified a core stdio MCP server configured through `mcp.servers.*.env.*` receives resolved string env values at launch time while the config itself still stores SecretRef objects
- verified custom credential-like names such as `SERVICE_KEY` and `X-Access-Key` are treated as sensitive by configure/audit flows
- verified generic literals such as URLs and feature-flag headers are not promoted as secret targets

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: `mcp.servers.*.env.*` and `mcp.servers.*.headers.*` only accepted primitive string literals before this PR. Passing a SecretRef object (`{"source":"env","id":"MC_API_KEY"}`) as an MCP env or header value caused `config validate` to return `Invalid input`. This PR widens the accepted surface so both `env` and `headers` fields on core MCP servers store SecretInput values, with runtime resolution delivering the resolved string to the spawned MCP process.

- Real environment tested: Ubuntu 24.04 (HAL server), OpenClaw built from PR head `24e3416d75b` (runtime captured at parent `9598ab1` — `24e3416d75b` changes test-file module paths only, no runtime delta). 1Password CLI service account for secret backing.

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Write `openclaw.json` with `mcp.servers.mission-control.env.MC_API_KEY = {"source":"env","id":"MC_API_KEY"}` and `mcp.servers.mission-control.headers.Authorization = {"source":"env","id":"MC_AUTH_TOKEN"}`
  2. `openclaw config validate`
  3. `openclaw secrets audit` (env vars absent — SecretRefs unresolved)
  4. `MC_API_KEY=[REDACTED] MC_AUTH_TOKEN=[REDACTED] ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED] openclaw secrets audit`

- Evidence after fix (copied terminal output, values redacted):

  ```
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (9598ab1)

  $ openclaw config validate
  Config valid: /tmp/proof/state/openclaw.json

  $ openclaw secrets audit
  Secrets audit: unresolved. plaintext=0, unresolved=3, shadowed=0, legacy=0.
  - [REF_UNRESOLVED] openclaw.json:mcp.servers.mission-control.env.MC_API_KEY
      Failed to resolve env:default:MC_API_KEY (variable missing)
  - [REF_UNRESOLVED] openclaw.json:mcp.servers.mission-control.headers.Authorization
      Failed to resolve env:default:MC_AUTH_TOKEN (variable missing)
  - [REF_UNRESOLVED] openclaw.json:models.providers.anthropic.apiKey
      Failed to resolve env:default:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (variable missing)

  $ MC_API_KEY=[REDACTED] MC_AUTH_TOKEN=[REDACTED] ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED] openclaw secrets audit
  Secrets audit: clean. plaintext=0, unresolved=0, shadowed=0, legacy=0.
  ```

- Observed result after fix: Config validates cleanly with SecretRef objects in both `env.*` and `headers.*`. Secrets audit identifies `MC_API_KEY` and `Authorization` as unresolved SecretRefs and correctly ignores `MC_URL` (URL-shaped) and `X-Feature-Flag` (generic literal). With env vars set, audit is fully clean (`plaintext=0, unresolved=0`).

- What was not tested: Live end-to-end MCP spawn with SecretRef values resolved from exec provider (HAL `/tmp` is mounted `noexec`, blocking shell-script exec tests locally). MCP session runtime SecretRef injection is covered by unit tests in `pi-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`.

- Proof limitations or environment constraints: `/tmp` is mounted `noexec` on the test machine, preventing exec-provider shell-script invocation locally. Same exec tests pass in CI (GitHub Actions standard tmpfs is executable). Version shown is `9598ab1` (parent of `24e3416d75b`) — both commits produce identical runtime behavior; `24e3416d75b` only renames test-file module paths.

- Before evidence: Without this PR, `openclaw config validate` on the same config returned:
  ```
  OpenClaw config is invalid: /tmp/proof/state/openclaw.json
    x mcp.servers.mission-control.env.MC_API_KEY: Invalid input
    x mcp.servers.mission-control.headers.Authorization: Invalid input
  ```

## Scope

This PR is limited to core MCP SecretRef support for `mcp.servers` env/header surfaces and the related docs/tests needed to support that behavior.

It does not include unrelated runtime, deployment, or integration changes.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): Add group admin privacy controls
target.body:
Closes #69233

## What changed

This adds an optional per-group WhatsApp admin override via `channels.whatsapp.groups.<jid>.admin` and wildcard `channels.whatsapp.groups."*".admin`.

When an admin is configured for a group scope:
- the configured E.164 number bypasses mention gating for that group
- non-admin group members cannot run slash commands in that group
- the configured admin remains able to run slash commands for that group

When no admin is configured, the existing group command authorization behavior is preserved.

## Why

The issue described a privacy gap in mixed-trust WhatsApp groups: non-admin members could still probe bot behavior through mentions and slash commands. The first pass of this feature covered the basic config and enforcement, but upstream readiness also needed the behavior pinned down for wildcard group config and for the no-admin-configured fallback path.

## User impact

Users can now designate a WhatsApp group admin by phone number and use that as a privacy boundary for command discovery in group chats.

This is intentionally backwards-compatible:
- groups without `admin` continue using the existing command authorization rules
- exact-group and wildcard group config both work
- docs now describe the new config key

## Root cause

OpenClaw already had group policy, allowlists, and mention gating, but it did not have a per-group owner/admin concept for WhatsApp. That meant there was no narrow way to let a trusted operator manage the bot in a group without exposing command access to other participants covered by broader allowlist rules.

## Validation

target.title: fix(gateway): prefer current route delivery context
target.body:
## Summary

- Fixes gateway agent delivery resolution so a concrete current request route (`channel`, `to`, `accountId`, `threadId`) wins over stale persisted session `deliveryContext` fields when the channels conflict.
- Clears stale route fields on channel switches when the new request does not provide replacement `to`/`accountId`/`threadId` values, avoiding mixed-channel routes.
- Preserves existing session-route behavior for normal follow-ups, `channel=last`, and same-channel existing-session routes.
- Compares same-channel targets through the channel parser so equivalent encodings do not clear stored threads.
- Populates `runContext.currentChannelId` from the resolved delivery target so downstream message-tool fallback inference sees the active route.
- Adds regression tests for the #68378 shape, channel-only stale-route clearing, same-channel partial updates, and canonical equivalent targets.

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #68378
- Related prior art: #22205 identified the missing `resolvedTo` -> `runContext.currentChannelId` propagation, but that PR is closed unmerged and does not address stale delivery-context precedence.
- Related but not duplicates: #45514, #65847, #33619, #39557, #51812, #52204 all describe adjacent multi-channel/stale-routing problems or other delivery paths; none is an open satisfactory PR for this gateway agent route-precedence bug.

## Root Cause / Diagnosis

`src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts` built `requestDeliveryHint` from the active gateway request, but then merged it with the stored session `deliveryContext` in a way that made persisted fields authoritative. That let stale persisted fields, such as Feishu `channel`/`to`, override a current Discord request before the agent command and session update were assembled. The same path also did not pass the resolved target into `runContext.currentChannelId`, so tool fallback routing could miss the current route even when `resolvedTo` was known.

A second edge case appears when the request changes only `channel`: route-field fallback must not pair a new channel with stale `lastTo`/`lastAccountId`/`lastThreadId` from the old channel.

A third edge case appears when the request and session refer to the same target with different channel-owned encodings, such as Slack `C1` and `channel:C1`: raw string comparison can falsely treat that as a target change and clear the stored thread.

## Fix

- Detect when a concrete request channel conflicts with the stored session delivery channel.
- In that cross-channel conflict case, let the current request delivery hint win and use persisted delivery metadata only as fallback for fields provided by the current route.
- Clear stale last-route fields when the current channel conflicts and no replacement field is available.
- For same-channel route conflicts, preserve unchanged target/account/thread fields unless the concrete target itself changes.
- Compare request/session targets using the channel parser before treating `to` as a target change, preserving stored threads for equivalent target spellings.
- For non-conflict cases, keep existing session delivery precedence so `channel=last`, normal follow-ups, and existing subagent routes behave as before.
- Pass `resolvedTo` into `runContext.currentChannelId` alongside the existing channel/account/thread context.
- Lock the behavior with regression tests that start from stale Feishu metadata, assert Discord wins or stale route fields are cleared, preserve partial same-channel updates, and keep Slack threads when `C1` and `channel:C1` are equivalent.

## Duplicate Sweep

Searched GitHub issues/PRs for combinations of `#68378`, Discord/Feishu wrong-channel delivery, stale `deliveryContext`, gateway agent delivery, `currentChannelId`, and multi-channel session routing. Closest results:

- #22205: overlapping `currentChannelId` propagation only; closed unmerged; no stale context precedence fix or regression for #68378.
- #35451: broader `chat.send`/cron canonical route derivation; closed unmerged; different call sites.
- #67508: target-agent bound account propagation for Matrix subagent spawns; adjacent account routing, different bug.
- #45514, #65847, #33619, #39557, #51812, #52204: related issue reports/bug class, not acceptable duplicate PRs for this exact gateway agent request-route overwrite.

Conclusion: no duplicate or already-satisfactory PR found for #68378.

## Attribution

- Thanks @Suidge for the #68378 report and follow-up logs that isolated Discord input being delivered through Feishu outbound.
- Thanks @Galygious for prior analysis in #22205 around forwarding `resolvedTo` into `runContext.currentChannelId`; this PR incorporates that same missing-context piece and adds the route-precedence fix needed for #68378.

## Testing

Fresh `origin/main` base: `64089fd15ed4ba8296612b1a622d11b5662c8b96`

- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts -t "uses the current request route"`
- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts`
- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts -t "preserves the stored thread when the request target is canonically equivalent"`
- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-a.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-b.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent.subagent-delivery-context.test.ts`

The final command covers the CI shard failures observed after the first draft and now passes locally with 71 tests.

Scoped lint note: `pnpm lint -- src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` is currently blocked before linting these files by the existing `src/agents/skills/*` plugin SDK boundary type errors already present on `origin/main`.

## Review Follow-up

- Addressed and resolved Codex review thread about clearing stale route fields on channel-switch merges in `5825aede6c7568f8cec2af2653d4851bf3296d78`.
- Addressed and resolved Codex review thread about preserving unchanged same-channel route fields in `d8f4d09a343f30d82df2bdeea9541a707923a72d`.
- Addressed and resolved Codex review thread about canonical target comparison in `af7506771a0fd734024ecc2b51b23b7945f27b21`.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

The change narrows routing behavior to prefer the active request route only when it conflicts with stale persisted delivery metadata, and preserves stored thread context for equivalent same-channel target spellings.

target.title: fix(cron): warn when --system-event on main session contains shell commands
target.body:
## Summary

- `cron add --system-event "./run.sh" --session main` and similar commands used to create or edit the job silently even though main-session system events do not execute shell commands.
- Adds a shared `looksLikeShellCommand()` helper for common runtimes and relative script paths such as `./run.sh`.
- Emits a non-blocking warning before `cron.add` / `cron.update` when the effective session target is `main`, the payload is `systemEvent`, and the text looks like a shell command.

Fixes #63107

## Root Cause

System events on the main session are dispatched as context notifications to the agent. They are not executed as shell commands, so shell-looking `--system-event` payloads on `--session main` were silently non-functional.

## Changes

- `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts`: Adds the shared shell-command heuristic.

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction always shares the session's current thinking level. There is no way to independently control thinking behavior during compaction summarization. Users who want to save tokens/cost during compaction or avoid thinking artifacts in summaries had no option to disable thinking for compaction alone.

This adds `agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel` config option. When set, compaction uses this thinking level instead of the session's current level. Precedence: explicit `params.thinkLevel` > `config.compaction.thinkingLevel` > `"off"` (default).

## Evidence

**Proxy log evidence** (request 907 — compaction summarization call, model Qwen3.6-27B-FP8):

Request body:
```json
{
  "model": "Qwen3.6-27B-FP8",
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": {
    "include_usage": true
  },
  "max_completion_tokens": 16000
}
```

Response:
```json
{
  "id": "chatcmpl-986428eb-dc58-4a7d-bc2d-881504084088",
  "choices": [{
    "index": 0,
    "delta": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "...compaction summary...",
      "reasoning_content": null,

    "finish_reason": "stop"
  }],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 289,
    "total_tokens": 648,

}
```

- `enable_thinking` not present in request body → API defaults to thinking off

target.title: fix(browser): bound CDP JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.ts:309` calls raw `response.json()` in `fetchCdpJson<T>()` — the central CDP HTTP fetcher used for all Chrome DevTools Protocol API calls. CDP communicates with a local Chrome instance over `localhost:PORT`. Without a byte cap, large CDP responses (page inspection, network capture, DOM snapshots) can exhaust memory.

`extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.diagnostics.ts:113` calls raw `response.json()` in `readChromeVersion` — the diagnostics path for Chrome version probing.

**Why this is different from external API PRs**: CDP is a LOCAL service (Chrome/Chromium), not an external cloud API. Localhost-based proof is accepted, same as #98073 (signal container REST).

**Alix-007 has zero coverage of the browser module.**

## Changes

- `cdp.helpers.ts`: replace `response.json()` with `readResponseWithLimit` capped at 16 MiB in `fetchCdpJson`
- `chrome.diagnostics.ts`: replace `response.json()` with `readResponseWithLimit` capped at 16 MiB in `readChromeVersion`
- `cdp.helpers.test.ts`: migrate plain-object mock to `new Response()` for `readResponseWithLimit` compatibility
- `chrome.test.ts`: migrate all remaining CDP fetch mocks to `new Response()` objects (9 sites across 6 test cases)
- `test/_proof_cdp_bounded_json.mts`: real HTTP server proof script

## Evidence

### Unit tests: cdp.helpers.test.ts

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Unit tests: chrome.test.ts

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  50 passed (50)
```

### Real HTTP server proof

```
$ node --import tsx test/_proof_cdp_bounded_json.mts
PASS  oversized CDP response: throws Error :: type=Error
PASS  oversized CDP response: message mentions CDP JSON :: msg=CDP JSON response too large: 16842580 bytes (limit: 16777216 bytes)
PASS  normal CDP response: parsed correctly :: result={"ok":true,"id":"42"}

[proof] 3 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

### Cap rationale

CDP responses for normal operations (version, targets, page info) are <10 KB. Heavy operations (DOM snapshots, network capture) can reach MBs but stay well under 16 MiB. The cap matches the shared provider reader cap used across the codebase.

target.title: feat: configurable default agent ID (escape the 'main' prison) 🦞
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for overriding the hardcoded `"main"` fallback agent ID, so users with a single custom-named agent no longer get a ghost `agents/main/` default path/session identity when no `agents.list` is configured.

## The Problem

`DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` falls back to `"main"`. Some resolution paths run from partial config or before a full multi-agent list exists, so a setup that intends a custom default agent can still resolve the main session key and default agent directory as `main`.

## Solution

Two complementary override mechanisms:

### 1. Config key: `agents.defaultAgentId`

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaultAgentId": "maine-lobster"
  }
}
```

### 2. Env var: `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID`

```bash
export OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID=maine-lobster
```

### Priority (highest → lowest)

1. `agents.list[].default: true` (explicit default agent)
2. `agents.list[0]` (first configured agent)
3. `agents.defaultAgentId` config key
4. `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` env var
5. Hardcoded `"main"` (backward compatible)

## Changes

- Adds `agents.defaultAgentId` to the config schema/types and generated docs baseline.
- Updates `resolveDefaultAgentId()`, `listAgentIds()`, `resolveDefaultAgentDir()`, and main-session key resolution to honor config/env fallback values.
- Keeps populated `agents.list` behavior unchanged: list default/first entry still wins.
- Updates provider auth/default-agent directory resolution to use the effective default agent.
- Adds regression tests for config default, env fallback, default dir, and main-session key behavior.

## Testing

- `pnpm config:schema:check`
- `pnpm config:docs:check`
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope-config.test.ts src/config/sessions/main-session.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-key.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.apply.plugin-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm check:changed`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main` → merge-clean

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: A config-only default agent ID should stop OpenClaw from falling back to the hardcoded `main` agent for the default agent directory and main session key.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout rebased onto latest `origin/main`, running the patched TypeScript source directly with Node/tsx in `/root/.openclaw/workspace/openclaw-pr-acpx/pr-51762`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { resolveDefaultAgentId, resolveDefaultAgentDir } from './src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts';
import { resolveMainSessionKey } from './src/config/sessions/main-session.ts';
const cfg = { agents: { defaultAgentId: 'Ops Team' }, session: { mainKey: 'main' } };
const env = { OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: '/tmp/openclaw-real-proof' };
console.log('defaultAgentId=' + resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg, env));
console.log('defaultAgentDir=' + resolveDefaultAgentDir(cfg, env));
console.log('mainSessionKey=' + resolveMainSessionKey(cfg, env));
EOF
```

target.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` to control which agents a specific agent may contact via session tools (`sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `session_status`)
- When unset, the agent falls back to the global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` list; when set to explicit IDs, only those targets are reachable; `[]` isolates the agent from all cross-agent access
- The global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` continues to act as a participation gate (both requester and target must match it) before per-agent outbound rules are evaluated
- Outbound-only semantics: only the requester's override is checked, not the target's
- Replace `matchesAllow` with `matchesGlobalParticipation` and add `evaluateAccess()` returning a structured `AgentToAgentDenyReason` so all call sites produce context-aware error messages via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`
- Scrub deleted agent references from per-agent outbound allowlists in `pruneAgentConfig()`

### Example config (hub-spoke pattern)

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "david",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["*"] } } },
      { "id": "spoke",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } },
      { "id": "kelly",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } }
    ]
  }
}
```

spoke→david ✅ | spoke→kelly ❌ | david→anyone ✅

## Test plan

- [x] `sessions-access.test.ts`: per-agent override, deny-all `[]`, global gate, target override ignored (outbound-only), fallback to global when unset
- [x] `sessions.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny during label lookup in `sessions_send`
- [x] `openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny for cross-agent `session_status`
- [x] `agents.test.ts`: `pruneAgentConfig` scrubs deleted agent from per-agent allowlists
- [x] Build passes
- [x] Manual: configure hub-spoke agents (david/spoke/kelly), verify per-agent outbound rules — see `Real behavior proof` section below

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: per-agent outbound `agentToAgent.allow` correctly gates cross-agent session tool access. Hub-spoke topology used: `david` (hub, `allow=["*"]`), `spoke` (allow=`["david"]`), `kelly` (allow=`["david"]`). Validates the new `evaluateAccess()` decision pipeline reaches the documented per-agent outbound semantics, with the structured `per_agent_outbound` deny reason surfaced via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`.

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 5.15), Node 22.22.0, pnpm 10. Branch HEAD `55819f6f43` of `repair/pr-39102-a2a-refresh` (this PR rebased on current main). Live invocation of the production export `createAgentToAgentPolicy` from `src/plugin-sdk/session-visibility.ts` — no mocks, no test runner, the same code path that backs `sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `session_status` at runtime.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Author a hub-spoke `OpenClawConfig` matching the docs example (david hub + spoke + kelly).
  2. Build `policy = createAgentToAgentPolicy(cfg)`.
  3. Call `policy.evaluateAccess(requester, target)` for the five edge pairs.
  4. Run with: `pnpm tsx proof-hub-spoke.ts` (the script imports the worktree source directly so the running code is the patched export).

- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output, copied verbatim from `node` stdout via `tsx`.

  ```
  # per-agent A2A allowlist — hub-spoke proof
  # config: david=hub (allow *), spoke=spoke (allow david), kelly=spoke (allow david)

  [ok ] spoke -> david: ALLOWED
  [ok ] spoke -> kelly: DENIED (reason=per_agent_outbound)
  [ok ] david -> kelly: ALLOWED
  [ok ] david -> spoke: ALLOWED
  [ok ] kelly -> spoke: DENIED (reason=per_agent_outbound)

  all cases match expected behavior
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: all five real invocations matched the documented hub-spoke semantics. Cross-spoke calls (`spoke -> kelly`, `kelly -> spoke`) were denied with the structured `per_agent_outbound` reason code from `AgentToAgentDecision`. Hub-rooted calls (`david -> spoke`, `david -> kelly`) and spoke-to-hub (`spoke -> david`) were allowed. Process exit code: `0`. Console output above is the literal stdout, no post-processing.

- **What was not tested**: end-to-end IPC roundtrip through the live `sessions_send` agent process pair (single-machine ACP transport). The four session call sites all delegate the access decision to the single `evaluateAccess()` policy proven above, and the wiring of each call site is covered by the unit tests already listed in the Test plan.

target.title: feat(agents): expose tools and their schemas via new after_tools_resolved hook [AI-assisted]
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Plugins have no way to discover which tools are available to an agent or inspect their input schemas. The plugin API exposes `registerTool()` but no `listTools()` or `getTools()`. Built-in tools (exec, read, write, web_fetch, etc.) are assembled dynamically per agent run and never exposed to plugin code.
- **Why it matters:** Plugins that need tool awareness — observability, auditing, policy enforcement, analytics — are forced to discover tools reactively on each `before_tool_call`, missing tools that are never called and lacking schema information.
- **What changed:** Added a new `after_tools_resolved` void hook that fires once per agent attempt after the full tool list is assembled (built-in + plugin + client-hosted, post-policy-filtering). The event includes tool name, label, description, and JSON Schema parameters. Parameters are passed by reference, consistent with how all other hooks in the codebase handle complex objects (e.g., `messages` in `llm_input`, `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`).
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No existing hooks or tool assembly logic modified. Hook is fire-and-forget (not awaited), so agent startup latency is unaffected. Not fired during compaction runs.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR
* https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/21330
* https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/discussions/26940

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New plugin hook `after_tools_resolved` available via `api.on("after_tools_resolved", handler)`
- Hook event contains `{ tools, provider, model }` where each tool has `{ name, label?, description?, parameters? }`
- Parameters are passed by reference (consistent with all other hooks — no defensive cloning)
- Hook context includes `agentId`, `sessionKey`, `sessionId`, `workspaceDir`
- Fire-and-forget: plugin handler errors are caught and logged, never block agent startup

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No` — read-only observability hook, no new capabilities granted
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — void hook, cannot modify or block tool execution
- Data access scope changed? `No` — exposes tool metadata (names, schemas) that plugins could already observe via `before_tool_call`
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu (remote VM)
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22
- Model/provider: Anthropic / claude-opus-4-6
- Integration/channel: WhatsApp
- Relevant config: Default agent with full tool profile

### Steps

1. Create a workspace plugin at `{workspaceDir}/.openclaw/extensions/test-tools-hook/`:

   `openclaw.plugin.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "id": "test-tools-hook",
     "configSchema": {
       "type": "object",
       "additionalProperties": false,
       "properties": {}
     }
   }
   ```

   `index.ts`:
   ```typescript
   export default function testToolsHook(api) {
     api.on("after_tools_resolved", async (event, ctx) => {
       const toolNames = event.tools.map((t) => t.name).join(", ");
       console.log(`[test-tools-hook] agent=${ctx.agentId} provider=${event.provider} model=${event.model}`);
       console.log(`[test-tools-hook] ${event.tools.length} tools resolved: ${toolNames}`);
       for (const tool of event.tools) {
         const params = tool.parameters?.properties
           ? Object.keys(tool.parameters.properties).join(", ")
           : "(no schema)";
         console.log(`  - ${tool.name}: ${params}`);
       }
     });
   }
   ```

2. Restart the gateway: `openclaw gateway --force --verbose`
3. Send a WhatsApp message to trigger an agent run

### Expected

- Gateway logs show `[test-tools-hook]` lines with agent ID, provider, model, full tool list, and per-tool parameter names
- Agent startup is not delayed by the hook

### Actual

- Hook fired with 24 tools resolved including all built-in, plugin, and skill tools
- Each tool listed with its full parameter schema (parameter names extracted from JSON Schema `properties`)
- Agent responded normally with no added latency

## Evidence

**New unit tests pass:**

- `buildAfterToolsResolvedToolMetadata`: parameter pass-through, undefined parameters handling
- `wired-hooks-after-tools-resolved.test.ts`: hook runner invocation, `hasHooks` registration

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Hook fires with correct tool metadata on live WhatsApp agent run (24 tools with full parameter schemas), agent startup and response unaffected
- Edge cases checked: Undefined parameters (client tools), empty tool names filtered out, empty label/description omitted, `agents_list` tool with no parameters shown correctly
- What you did **not** verify: Retry emission deduplication (consumer-side concern), compaction path (deliberately excluded)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes` — purely additive, no existing behavior changed
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert this commit. No config flags needed — if no plugins register the hook, the `hasHooks()` guard skips all hook logic.
- Files/config to restore: N/A
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Unhandled promise rejections in gateway logs (mitigated by explicit `.catch()` on the fire-and-forget call)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Hook fires per attempt, not per user request (retries cause repeated emissions)
  - Mitigation: By design — each attempt is a fresh tool resolution. Consumers should dedupe if needed (e.g., hash-based caching). Documented in hook description.

target.title: fix(status): LINE /status intermittent no-response — fallback, timeout, and retry hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes LINE `/status` intermittently returning no response by hardening the dynamic module loaders, adding a safety-net timeout, and fixing CI failures.

### Changes (14 commits, +325/-64 across 12 files)

#### Core Status Fixes

| Phase | What | Rationale |
|:------|:-----|:---------|
| **Phase 0+1** | `.catch(() => undefined)` fallbacks on all 4 dynamic runtime loaders | Previously, a transient import failure would propagate uncaught — now each loader returns sensible defaults instead of throwing |
| **Phase 2** | Eliminate 2 fragile dynamic-import wrappers (`status-message.runtime.ts`, `status-queue.runtime.ts`) via precise static imports; fix `??=` cached-rejection on remaining 3 loaders by resetting promise to `null` on reject | Static imports eliminate the dynamic-hop failure point; promise reset removes the permanent-cache poison so transient failures are retried |
| **Phase 2 fix** | Replace `?? {} as any` false-positive in plugin health line with proper early-return guard | Previously a loader failure would show "🔌Plugins: OK" instead of "🔌 Plugins: health unavailable" |
| **Phase 3** | Add 10s `setTimeout` race in `buildStatusReply` | Without the timeout, a hanging render produces zero response to the user |
| **ClawSweeper fixes** | Revert `warn` → `logVerbose` in `logLineHttpError` (P1); delete committed proof image (P2); add standalone proof scripts (P3) | `warn` is a theme formatter, not a logger — LINE HTTP errors were invisible |

#### CI Fixes

| Fix | What | Rationale |
|:----|:-----|:---------|
| **OOM mitigation** | Set `OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_PARALLEL=1` for core-tooling CI shard | Prevents OOM (2x8GB vitest processes on 16GB runner) |
| **Guard test fix** | Update `ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` assertion to match the GHA ternary expression | Fixes pre-existing test that validated the old hardcoded `"2"` value |

#### Tests

| Suite | Tests | Coverage |
|:------|:------|:---------|
| `commands-status.test.ts` | 19 | Timeout path (new), throw path, and all existing scenarios |
| `status-text.test.ts` | 7 | `??=` retry pattern (new, fail → retry → succeed), channel features, plugin health |
| `send.test.ts` | 14 | Updated assertions for `logVerboseMock` (P1 fix) |
| `task-registry.test.ts` | 77 | All upstream tests pass after rebase |

### Closes

Closes openclaw/openclaw#94626

---

### Types of Changes

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation (non-code change that improves documentation)
- [ ] 🔧 Chore (refactoring, test updates, CI configuration changes)

---

## What Problem This Solves

LINE `/status` command intermittently returned no response when dynamic imports through the `??=` pattern suffered a transient failure — the rejected promise was cached permanently, causing every subsequent `/status` attempt to hang indefinitely. Additionally, the timeout safety net was missing entirely: if any segment of the status rendering stalled, the user received zero response.

---

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:**
- **OS:** Windows 11 24H2
- **Runtime:** Node.js v24.14.1
- **Branch:** `fix/line-94626-status` (rebased onto upstream/main `e9720c27fa`)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
node scripts/status-timeout-proof.mjs
node scripts/status-retry-proof.mjs
```

**Evidence after fix — timeout fallback:**
```
=== /status Timeout Fallback Proof ===
Testing: buildStatusReply with simulated hanging buildStatusText
Result: Status render timeout after 518ms
Elapsed: 518ms
=== Proof Complete ===
```

**Evidence after fix — retry pattern:**
```
=== /status Dynamic Import Retry Proof ===
Call 1 (should fail with undefined, promise cache reset):
  Result: undefined (promise was reset)
  loaderPromise after call 1: null (ready for retry)
Call 2 (should succeed after retry):
  Result: {"default":"status-module-loaded"}
  loaderPromise after call 2: set (cached)
Test result: PASSED
```

**Observed result after fix:** Both proof scripts pass — timeout fallback triggers within 518ms and returns a user-visible message instead of hanging forever; the `??=` retry pattern gracefully handles a transient import failure, resets the promise cache, and succeeds on a subsequent retry.

**What was not tested:**
- Cross-platform runtime testing (Windows 11 only)
- The core-tooling OOM fix can only be verified in CI (runner resource constraints)

---

target.title: fix(openai): enable prompt cache keys for Azure
target.body:
## Summary
- centralize Azure OpenAI chat-completions prompt-cache-key detection in the shared completions compat defaults
- apply that default in the legacy provider builder, boundary-aware OpenAI transport, and embedded-agent extra-params retention eligibility path
- include traditional Azure hosts, Azure AI Foundry project hosts, and regional `.api.cognitive.microsoft.com` Foundry hosts
- preserve Azure long prompt-cache retention (`prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`) when callers request `cacheRetention: "long"`, and preserve explicit `cacheRetention: "none"`
- add regression coverage for Azure prompt-cache key emission, long/disabled retention, extra-params propagation, and both request paths

## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw already gates OpenAI-compatible prompt cache keys behind `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey`, but Azure OpenAI chat-completions endpoints were not auto-detected. Azure users therefore needed explicit per-model compat config before stable session prompt-cache keys were forwarded, which can silently reduce prompt-cache hit opportunities for long stable prefixes.

The change treats Azure OpenAI chat-completions endpoints (`azure-openai`, `.openai.azure.com`, `.cognitiveservices.azure.com`, `.services.ai.azure.com`, and `.api.cognitive.microsoft.com`) as prompt-cache-key capable by default. The default now lives in the shared completions compat path used by both request builders and by embedded-agent extra-param cache-retention eligibility; explicit `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey` / `compat.supportsLongCacheRetention` overrides continue to win.

## Evidence
- Searched existing issues/PRs before filing. Found related prompt-cache work (#78747, #82939, #94518, #83709, #69272, #67427), but no open PR specifically enabling Azure OpenAI chat-completions prompt cache keys by default.
- Verified upstream `main` only enabled chat-completions `prompt_cache_key` for `api.openai.com` or explicit `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey`; Azure endpoint detection was absent in both relevant request paths and extra-params retention eligibility.
- Added regression tests that confirm Azure OpenAI chat completions forward `prompt_cache_key`, preserve `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"` for long retention, preserve `cacheRetention: "none"`, cover the regional Azure Foundry host, and propagate embedded-agent `cacheRetention` for detected Azure models.
- Live Azure proof, redacted terminal output from `thomais2026v2-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/chat/completions` using `gpt-5.5`, `prompt_cache_key`, and `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`:

target.title: fix(whatsapp): add listGroupsLive for real-time group directory
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves The WhatsApp channel directory adapter only registered `listGroups` (which reads from the config map `channels.whatsapp.groups`) but did **not** register `listGroupsLive`. The CLI (and other consumers) prefer `listGroupsLive` when available, so users who have active WhatsApp group memberships but an empty config-based groups map would see `No groups found.` from `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`. Fixes #76722 ## Why This Change Was Made This PR adds `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsLive` that fetches groups from the Baileys socket via `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. The function has two code paths: 1. **Process-local controller** (gateway process): uses the existing `getRegisteredWhatsAppConnectionController()` socket — the fast path when a gateway is running. 2. **Standalone socket** (CLI process): when no process-local controller exists (e.g. `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp` as a standalone command), opens a temporary Baileys socket using stored auth credentials from disk, fetches group metadata, then closes the socket. Both paths fall back gracefully to the config-backed `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsFromConfig` on failure. ## User Impact WhatsApp users who have joined groups but haven't manually configured them in `channels.whatsapp.groups` can now see their real group memberships in the directory — from both the gateway process and the standalone CLI. No config changes required. ## Evidence - `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/directory-config.test.ts` — 11/11 passed - `pnpm tsgo:test` — passed - Lint + format — passed - Rebased onto `upstream/main` — resolves unrelated CI failures in `check-lint`, `check-test-types` **Real behavior proof** — Linux, Node 24.13.1, commit `0a7ae017e3`, linked WhatsApp account (phone number redacted). Standalone CLI `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`: ```console $ openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp Groups (4) ┌────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐ │ ID │ Name │ ├────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┤ │ 120363409866058990@g.us │ openclaw_test │ │ 120363409260302345@g.us │ General │ │ 120363408822325057@g.us │ openclaw_test │ │ 120363408212902124@g.us │ test_group │ └────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘ ``` 4 groups returned from `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. WhatsApp phone app shows 3 groups — `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group`. The API returns 4 entries because `openclaw_test` is a WhatsApp Community which Baileys represents as two separate group JIDs (announcement + sub-group). This is expected protocol-level behavior. > **🖼️ WhatsApp app shows 3 groups: `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group` What was not tested: Crabbox cross-platform proof. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(ui): bridge tool stream state to composer run status indicator
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the agent is actively running tools, the Activity panel correctly shows "Activity: N tools Exec" with a spinner, but the composer area displays no "In progress" indicator and no Stop button — appearing completely idle. Users cannot tell whether the agent is working or has stalled.

Root cause: the composer's in-progress state is driven exclusively by `chatRunId` and `sessionsResult[].hasActiveRun`, while the Activity panel uses an independent agent event stream (`activityEntries[]`). There is no bridge between these two data paths. When `chatRunId` is cleared by a racing `sessions.changed` event (via `reconcileChatRunFromSessionRow()`) while tools are still streaming, the composer goes idle while Activity correctly shows running tools.

Fixes #98540

## Changes

- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.ts`** — Add `hasActiveToolExecution()` and `resolveActiveToolRunId()` helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`** — Re-export the new helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-chat.ts`** — `hasAbortableSessionRun()` checks activity entries as third signal; `handleAbortChat()` falls back to tool stream runId
- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.test.ts`** — 9 unit tests for new helpers

## Evidence

**Test results (9 new + 26 existing pass without regression):**

✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is undefined ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is empty ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are done ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns true when at least one entry is running ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are error ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when activityEntries is undefined ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when no running entries ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the runId of the running entry ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the most recently updated running entry's runId


Existing `app-tool-stream.node.test.ts` (26 tests) pass without regression.

**Screenshot showing the bug:** See #98540 for screenshot evidence.
